claims.quote: Much which is now established in Soviet Russia bears at least a likeness to the industrial army visioned in this prophetic book.
claims.description: The book imagines a national industrial army that organizes all labor.

claims.quote: Some of the things which must have seemed most improbable of all to the *Transcript* man of 1887 are now actually in being.
claims.description: Improbable features of the book's imagined world have since become real.

claims.quote: its definite scheme of industrial organization on a national basis, and the equal share allotted to all persons in the products of industry
claims.description: Industry is organized nationally and all citizens receive an equal share of national output.

claims.quote: enjoying the blessings of a social order at once so simple and logical that it seems but the triumph of common sense
claims.description: Society is organized so simply and logically that it appears to be the triumph of common sense.

claims.quote: The long and weary winter of the race is ended. Its summer has begun. Humanity has burst the chrysalis.
claims.description: Humanity enters a new era of fraternal society and spiritual fulfillment after a long period of hardship.

claims.quote: Nowadays, as life advances toward its close, instead of being shadowed by gloom, it is marked by an access of impassioned expectancy
claims.description: Old age is marked by eager expectancy rather than gloom.
